To: lindqvist-family-blog
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: IT'S OFFICIAL: FERNHOLLOW PHOTO IS A REAL BUSINESS!!

Okay, I have been sitting on this for three weeks and it is time to just say it out loud: Fernhollow Photo is a real business. LLC filed. Website live. Fourteen weddings booked for 2027. FOURTEEN. I keep looking at that number like it's a typo, and it isn't.

Hi, I'm Tessa. I've been shooting weddings for four years, and as of October I'm doing it on my own, under my own name, which is the part I still can't quite believe.

THE NAME, FIRST

Grandma — this one's for you.

Fernhollow Photo is named after the fern hollow trail behind your old place in Gresham. When I was twelve you put your old Pentax in my hands and sent me down that trail with one instruction: "go take real pictures." Not pictures of me. Pictures of the moss and the light coming sideways through the trees. That was the first time I understood that a photograph isn't about what you put in front of the camera. I still have the Pentax. Sam keeps it on a shelf where I can see it, which is very generous of him, but he knows.

So if anybody has been wondering why there's an entire business named after a trail in Gresham, that's the reason. I'm telling you in person, with the good glasses, at Thanksgiving.

HOW THIS HAPPENED (the short version)

For four years I shot for Marisol at Rosebud Lane, and I want to say this part properly, because she earned it: Marisol taught me everything. Every single thing I know about lighting, about getting a nervous bride to laugh, about holding a lens for eleven hours and still having the energy to dance at the reception. She taught me how to run a wedding day, how to run a business, and how to be the person who makes everybody else look good. She deserves a shoutout, so: shoutout. Loudly. Right here. ★★★★★

Marisol is closing Rosebud Lane at the end of October, and she told me before she told almost anybody, which I still think about a lot. Six of my fourteen weddings for 2027 are couples she handed to me one at a time, along with the sentence "she's ready, trust her." So six of my fourteen are hers, in the way that a whole chunk of my actual career is hers.

I'm not going to say anything else about her plans, because that's her story to tell, whenever she wants to tell it. You'll hear it from her, and it will be better than anything I could say.

But she sent me Dahlia and Ken, and they were the first booking that was 100% mine. June 12 at Timberline. They found me from the photos I shot for Marisol's couple at Multnomah Falls — the ones down by the water with the fog doing that thing — and Dahlia emailed me a sentence that made me sit down: "we loved those photos, that's what sold us." I have that email saved. I will probably show it to strangers for the rest of my life.

THE PLAN

I know some of you are doing math right now (Dad, I know you're doing math, you are always doing math), so here is the plan, not the vibes:

• 14 weddings booked for 2027. June is my busiest month with four of them, and the furthest out is Wallowa Lake in September, which means I finally get to sleep in August. Once.
• Deposits are already in, so this isn't a dream on a napkin.
• Jae is second shooting the big weddings with me, and they're paid per wedding. One of the very nice things about being my own boss is that I can pay my people properly, from the very first one.
• Health insurance: SORTED. Yes, Dad, I know, you don't have to do the speech. Marketplace plan, starts January 1. Done. You're welcome. (You wanted to put Bree in a school portrait outfit, didn't you. I read the comment. She's got a baby, Dennis. She is not going back to school.)

And since somebody will ask: LLC filed October 22. At lunch. In the car, in the parking lot of a Fred Meyer, on my phone, because apparently I could not wait two more minutes. I cried a little. Then I went inside and bought bread and milk like a perfectly normal person, with Sam on speakerphone the whole time asking if I wanted him to come get me, and I said no and yes at the same time.

Is it scary? Yeah. Some days it's really scary, especially when I'm up at 5 a.m. in the dark driving to a house full of strangers and one extremely important dress.

But here's the thing: I didn't decide to do this last week. I've been planning it in my head for two years. Two years of spreadsheets (Dad, of course I had spreadsheets, I'm your daughter) and pricing out lenses and talking it through with Sam and running the numbers until it stopped feeling like a fantasy and started feeling like a plan. I'm not being reckless with this. I got tired of waiting to be ready, and then I got ready.

THE CAKE

Sam made a cake to celebrate and it said FERNHOLLOW. It did not. It said FERNHOLOW. We ate it anyway, because it was chocolate and you do not waste chocolate over a spelling mistake. Sam says hi, and he says I'm still not allowed to book anything on his birthday weekend. That rule exists for a reason and I have accepted it.

THANKSGIVING

Here's the actual business I need from you: I'm bringing the camera to Ruthie's on November 26 and I'm doing FREE FAMILY PICTURES. Free. No package, no album, no invoice, no minimum headcount. If you want a picture of your family, come find me. Bring the kids, bring the grandkids, bring Aunt Ruthie's dog if he tolerates strangers.

I have a plan for the light in the front room around four o'clock, and also for the yard, and also for whatever the cousins are wearing that makes everybody look great. If you have strong feelings about your outfit, wear it. If you have strong feelings about being photographed, drink the punch first and tell me later, I will work with you.

Also, Juniper Rose, seven pounds four ounces, is going to be the smallest member of the photo shoot and I am going to take her picture about nine hundred times. Bree, I'm sorry in advance.

Tell Ruthie I have the cranberry thing on the list, and that I'll be there at 1:45 with the camera before anybody else, because I am not allowed to be late.

SO

That's the announcement. Fernhollow Photo. My name on the website, my own calendar, my own terrifying invoice system, my own four years of learning.

If you know a couple getting married, send them my way. If you don't know any, that's fine too, but I will be gently persistent about it.

Bookings for fall 2027 open in February. Tell your friends.

Love you all. See you at Thanksgiving. Bring the good glasses, Grandma.

Tessa

P.S. Sam says hi.
P.P.S. The cake was still good.

[Note to self: saved as a draft, not published — delete this line before it goes live.]

Cc: none
Subject: the Fernhollow post (draft, not published yet)

Hi Marisol — I wrote the announcement for the family blog and I wanted you to read it before it goes anywhere. It's saved as a draft, nothing is live yet.

It says you taught me everything, because you did, and it mentions that Rosebud Lane is closing and that six of my 2027 couples came from you. Everything else I kept to myself, the way you asked. That's yours to tell, whenever you want to tell it, and I'll say nothing until you do.

If any of those six couples has a question about their date, they can call me and I'll loop you in. You know their stories better than I do, and I'd rather they had both of us.

The website is live if you want to see it. And yes, I cried in a Fred Meyer parking lot, so you can add that to the list of things you already knew about me.

Thank you for everything. I don't say it enough.
